_comment: Card ownership, granted by the controller. launch_gate reads launch_block_granted
and note; a false grant with no note reads as a stub, not as a decision.
Idle is not free: a card's owner is the job still running or the one the controller
has queued, never the instantaneous nvidia-smi row.
AND A STALE GRANT IS WORSE THAN NO GRANT (b0 2026-09-03): the 0-7 grant below outlived
the run it was made for, so the next launcher would have read it as licence to take
cards 4 and 7 -- which hold the USER'S OWN work in another container. The rule above
cuts both ways: a card's owner is not the nvidia-smi row, and it is not a superseded

lane_note: NO LANE as of the probes finishing. Card 5 was reclaimed by another container inside the release window -- b0 observed no measurable gap between his release and pid 862745 holding 38,778 MiB. That is the FOURTH instance that a named lane does not survive, and the shortest: the earlier ones were hours, then six minutes, then seconds, then no observable window at all. The rule is not 'read recently', it is READ AND CLAIM IN ONE ACTION, and when that is impossible, expect to lose the card and design the job to be restartable. Block stays 0-3.

lane_two_card_exception: GRANTED 2026-09-03, narrow, one job: de's dist.all_to_all_single microbench may hold BOTH lane cards at once. The 06:05Z widening was three jobs one card each and de read it correctly as not covering this. The exception is not 'big jobs may take two': it is that MEASURING A LINK REQUIRES TWO ENDPOINTS -- a two-rank all_to_all on one card is a device-to-device copy and measures nothing about NVLink, so there is no one-card version of this job to fall back to. Bounded by occupancy, not by importance: 110 MB x ~10 repeats is SECONDS. Any job that structurally needs two endpoints AND occupies seconds qualifies; a job that merely runs faster on two cards does not. ORDERING: card 6 is held IDLE until b0's score_matrix row on card 7 finishes, then de takes 6+7, then e1's pass@k starts on 6. Holding one card idle for the ~20 min of b0's row is the price of not queueing a seconds-long job behind an hours-long one -- a queue ordered by arrival makes the lane slower than no lane.
